article.title: Ubiquitous
article.description: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.
article.content: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.

Want to sound more advanced than 'everywhere'? ✨ Today's word, **Ubiquitous**, means something is present or found everywhere. It's perfect for formal writing, especially in IELTS essays, to elevate your vocabulary! For example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.'

generated.script: Everywhere ke liye ek behtar word chahiye? Yeh formal word aapke bahut kaam aayega! Toh aaj ka word hai ubiquitous. Isko pronounce karte hain yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Basically, iska matlab hai jo cheez har jagah ho, present everywhere. Jaise ki, 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Matlab smartphones ab modern life mein har jagah dikhte hain. Yeh ek formal word hai, specially IELTS writing mein use hota hai. Toh next time jab koi cheez har jagah dikhe, you can say it's ubiquitous! Kitna powerful word hai, right? slides.body: The word 'ubiquitous' (pronounced yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs) describes something that is present, appearing, or found everywhere. For example, 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life,' meaning they are found everywhere. This term is often used in formal or academic settings, making it particularly useful for IELTS Writing Task 2 essays when discussing topics like technology or globalization.
